prerequisites: Knowledge in mathematics and physics in a scope of the study at Faculty of Mechanical Engineering is expected.

learning_outcomes.text: Familiarize the students with the principles of the advanced electrical engineering which are necessary for the study of other mechanical engineering disciplines.

syllabus_topics: Introduction, basic elements, solutions of DC circuits ", basic circuit layout, basic elements, solutions of DC circuits
AC circuits, transient phenomena ", alternating quantities, passive elements in AC circuits, alternating circuit solutions, transient phenomena, three-phase quantities
Semiconductor devices ", semiconductors, diodes, transistors, thyristors
Power electronics ", rectifiers, converters, switched power supplies
Magnetic circuits, transformers ", magnetic materials, basic magnetic quantities, transformers
Rotating electrical machines, AC machines, synchronous machines, stepper motors, reluctance motors.
Asynchronous machines ", principle of function, properties, speed control, reversing, braking, single-phase asynchronous motors
DC machines ", principle of function, properties, speed control, electronically commutated motors, universal motors.
Electric drives ", structure of drives, loading characteristics, properties, efficiency, warming, calculation of equivalent drive parameters
Sensors with electrical output ", types of sensors, AD conversion, properties of measuring elements (sensors and inputs)
Electrical devices, electrical installations ", elements of electrical installation, protection, switching, safety
Electric drives ", drive control, modern electric drive
Application of electrical engineering in machines.
Introduction, administration affairs, safety at work.
Distribution of electrical energy
DC circuits and electronic elements.
AC electrical circuits.
Examples ", circuit
Electronic circuits.
Three-phase transformer.
Asynchronous machine.
Asynchronous motor with frequency converter.
DC motor.
Examples ", drives
Synchronous machine.
Application of contactors in practical terms, credit

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (theoretical part and part with examples)
All protocols processed and submitted in time and accepted by the teacher
Obtain at least half the number of points from the control tests
Presence of the students in laboratories
Each laboratory report shall be scored

assessment_rules: The course is completed by credit and exam. To gain the credit, students must meet conditions like compulsory attendance in laboratory, exercise preparation, timely submission and acceptance of protocols, and obtaining at least half the points from control tests. Control tests contribute a maximum of 20 points to the overall classification. The exam is a written test (theoretical part and examples) worth up to 80 points. The overall evaluation is based on the ECTS grading scale. Regularly apologized absences in laboratory practice may be compensated by attending with another team or an alternative practice at the end of the semester.
